1|High-Value Clinical Grammar Chunks.rule_explanation_en: Ready-made clinical chunks from the newborn-care dialogue: modal verbs for necessity, possibility and advice (need to, may, should, can), indirect questions that sound less abrupt (Could you tell me…?), and Present Perfect for symptoms since birth or since yesterday.
1|High-Value Clinical Grammar Chunks.rule_explanation_uz: Yangi tug'ilgan chaqaloq parvarishi dialogidan tayyor klinik konstruksiyalar: zarurat, ehtimol va maslahat uchun modal fe'llar (need to, may, should, can), yumshoqroq eshitiladigan bilvosita savollar (Could you tell me…?) va tug'ilgandan / kechadan beri kuzatilayotgan simptomlar uchun Present Perfect.
1|High-Value Clinical Grammar Chunks.rule_explanation_ru: Готовые клинические конструкции из диалога об уходе за новорождённым: модальные глаголы для необходимости, возможности и совета (need to, may, should, can), косвенные вопросы, звучащие мягче (Could you tell me…?), и Present Perfect для симптомов с рождения или со вчерашнего дня.

4|This — That.rule_explanation_en: THIS — one thing that is near or being discussed now. THAT — one thing that is further away or was mentioned earlier.
4|This — That.rule_explanation_ru: THIS — один предмет, который находится рядом или обсуждается сейчас. THAT — один предмет, который находится дальше или упоминался ранее.

4|These — Those.rule_explanation_en: THESE — several things that are near or being shown now. THOSE — several things that are further away or belong to another group.
4|These — Those.rule_explanation_ru: THESE — несколько предметов, которые находятся рядом или показываются сейчас. THOSE — несколько предметов, которые находятся дальше или относятся к другой группе.

4|Each vs Every.rule_explanation_en: EACH — every one considered separately (each lesion). EVERY — all members of a group as a whole (every child).
4|Each vs Every.rule_explanation_ru: EACH — каждый по отдельности (each lesion — каждое поражение). EVERY — все члены группы в целом (every child — каждый ребёнок).

6|Short Adjectives + -Er.rule_explanation_en: Adding -er to short adjectives: most one-syllable adjectives form the comparative by adding -er (small → smaller, high → higher).
6|Short Adjectives + -Er.rule_explanation_ru: Добавление -er к коротким прилагательным: большинство односложных прилагательных образуют сравнительную степень с помощью -er (small → smaller, high → higher).

6|Less + Adjective.rule_explanation_en: Structure: less + adjective shows that something has a quality to a smaller degree than something else (less severe, less frequent).
6|Less + Adjective.rule_explanation_ru: Структура: less + прилагательное показывает, что признак выражен слабее, чем у другого предмета (less severe, less frequent).

6|Irregular Forms.rule_explanation_en: Some adjectives do not follow the -er/-est or more/most rules: good → better → best, bad → worse → worst, far → further → furthest.
6|Irregular Forms.rule_explanation_ru: Некоторые прилагательные не подчиняются правилам -er/-est или more/most: good → better → best, bad → worse → worst, far → further → furthest.

7|Whose vs Where.rule_explanation_en: It is important not to confuse these two: WHOSE shows possession (a child whose speech is delayed), WHERE refers to a place (a clinic where children receive care).
7|Whose vs Where.rule_explanation_ru: Важно не путать эти два слова: WHOSE выражает принадлежность (a child whose speech is delayed), WHERE указывает на место (a clinic where children receive care).

7|Who vs Whose.rule_explanation_en: WHO gives information about the person (a doctor who assesses development). WHOSE gives information about something belonging to the person (a child whose speech is delayed).
7|Who vs Whose.rule_explanation_ru: WHO даёт информацию о самом человеке (a doctor who assesses development). WHOSE — о том, что принадлежит человеку (a child whose speech is delayed).

7|Clinical Communication Patterns.rule_explanation_en: The following constructions are very useful in medical English: relative clauses with who / which / that / whose / where to define the patient, the condition, the test or the place precisely in one sentence.
7|Clinical Communication Patterns.rule_explanation_ru: Следующие конструкции очень полезны в медицинском английском: придаточные с who / which / that / whose / where позволяют точно определить пациента, состояние, исследование или место в одном предложении.

7|High-Value Clinical Sentences.rule_explanation_en: Clinical sentences built with relative pronouns: a doctor who examines children; a condition that affects development; a child whose speech is delayed; a clinic where children receive care.
7|High-Value Clinical Sentences.rule_explanation_uz: Nisbiy olmoshlar bilan tuzilgan klinik gaplar: a doctor who examines children; a condition that affects development; a child whose speech is delayed; a clinic where children receive care.
7|High-Value Clinical Sentences.rule_explanation_ru: Клинические предложения с относительными местоимениями: a doctor who examines children; a condition that affects development; a child whose speech is delayed; a clinic where children receive care.

7|Quick Reference Table.rule_explanation_en: WHO — people; WHICH — things, conditions, symptoms, tests; THAT — people and things; WHOSE — possession (of whom); WHERE — place.
7|Quick Reference Table.rule_explanation_uz: WHO — odamlar; WHICH — narsalar, kasalliklar, simptomlar, tekshiruvlar; THAT — odamlar va narsalar; WHOSE — egalik (kimning); WHERE — joy.
7|Quick Reference Table.rule_explanation_ru: WHO — люди; WHICH — предметы, состояния, симптомы, исследования; THAT — люди и предметы; WHOSE — принадлежность (чей); WHERE — место.

8|Rapidly.rule_explanation_en: Rapidly shows that an action or a state happens very quickly (his condition can rapidly deteriorate).
8|Rapidly.rule_explanation_ru: Rapidly показывает, что действие или состояние происходит очень быстро (his condition can rapidly deteriorate).

8|Gradually.rule_explanation_en: Gradually shows that a change or development happens slowly, step by step (we will gradually increase the volume).
8|Gradually.rule_explanation_ru: Gradually показывает, что изменение или развитие происходит постепенно, шаг за шагом (we will gradually increase the volume).

8|Carefully.rule_explanation_en: Carefully shows that an action is performed with care or attention (we'll examine him carefully).
8|Carefully.rule_explanation_ru: Carefully показывает, что действие выполняется осторожно или внимательно (we'll examine him carefully).

8|While.rule_explanation_en: While shows that two actions or states happen at the same time (we monitor her while we assess her breathing).
8|While.rule_explanation_ru: While показывает, что два действия или состояния происходят одновременно (we monitor her while we assess her breathing).

9|Say → Said.rule_explanation_en: In Reported Speech, say usually becomes the past form said: The mother said that the child felt weak.
9|Say → Said.rule_explanation_ru: В косвенной речи say обычно принимает форму прошедшего времени said: The mother said that the child felt weak.

9|Tell → Told.rule_explanation_en: Tell normally requires the listener to be named: Subject + told + person + that + sentence. Difference between SAY and TELL: say + that, but tell + someone + that.
9|Tell → Told.rule_explanation_ru: Tell обычно требует указать, кому сказано: Subject + told + person + that + sentence. Разница между SAY и TELL: say + that, но tell + someone + that.

9|Explain → Explained.rule_explanation_en: Explain — to make something clear: The doctor explained that dizziness could indicate a significant clinical problem.
9|Explain → Explained.rule_explanation_ru: Explain — объяснить что-либо: The doctor explained that dizziness could indicate a significant clinical problem.

9|Report → Reported.rule_explanation_en: Report is a very important verb in medicine. It is used to convey clinical information formally: The nurse reported that his oxygen saturation was acceptable.
9|Report → Reported.rule_explanation_ru: Report — очень важный глагол в медицине. Он используется для официальной передачи клинической информации: The nurse reported that his oxygen saturation was acceptable.

10|\"in order to + verb\".rule_explanation_en: In order to also expresses purpose (in order to = so as to / for the purpose of): We examine him in order to identify the cause.
10|\"in order to + verb\".rule_explanation_ru: In order to также выражает цель (in order to = чтобы / с целью): We examine him in order to identify the cause.

10|Infinitive with key clinical structur.note_ru: need to + V to + V — действие ради другой цели
